verdicts.correction: The code-path facts are all confirmed: cookie 0.18.2 Cookie::domain() does strip_prefix(".") (lib.rs:777-785); wry cookie_into_win32 passes cookie.domain() to CreateCookie (mod.rs:1665-1668); tauri-runtime-wry set_cookie returns Ok(()) after posting the message, and the handler only calls log::error! (lib.rs:1698-1705, 3816-3826). It also returns Ok when the target webview no longer exists, because the message is dropped silently. The claim that a cookie stored with domain "roblox.com" is host-only and not sent to www/apis subdomains is still untested; Microsoft's doc only says the two strings are different domains. A live re-check today (GET https://www.roblox.com/login, no cookies) still returns rbx-ip2 and RBXEventTrackerV2 with domain=roblox.com, and GuestData with domain=.roblox.com, which matches the fixture.

The signatures are verified in webview2-com-sys 0.39.1. SetAreDefaultContextMenusEnabled, SetAreDevToolsEnabled, SetIsHttpOnly, SetIsSecure and SetAreBrowserAcceleratorKeysEnabled all take plain `bool`, and CreateCookie takes Param<PCWSTR>, so the sketch type-checks as written. One small correction: tauri-plugin-single-instance 2.5.4 uses windows-sys 0.61, not windows 0.62. tauri, wry, sysinfo and opener do use windows 0.62, and webview2-com 0.39.1 (2026-03-11) is current. Practical note: if the with_webview result is received through std mpsc from an async command, do the recv inside spawn_blocking or use a tokio oneshot, so a runtime worker is not blocked.

Two attribution fixes. (1) The 'Requires WebView2 Runtime version 101.0.1210.39' text is in wry 0.57 WebViewBuilder::with_incognito (wry lib.rs:1437), not in tauri's WebviewWindowBuilder::incognito doc. The same wry doc also says 'WebContext will be ignored if incognito is enabled', but on Windows wry still builds the environment from the data directory (webview2/mod.rs:293-351), so data_directory does apply together with incognito. (2) The tauri devtools doc says 'Enabled by default' and that it 'requires devtools feature flag to enable it in release builds'; tauri-runtime-wry gates it with cfg(any(debug_assertions, feature="devtools")). Also present but not listed: extensions_path, use_https_scheme, data_store_identifier (macOS-only), and scroll_bar_style. The grep confirms no profile_name, default_context_menus or browser_accelerator_keys plumbing in tauri 2.12.5 or tauri-runtime-wry 2.12.3.

The open question is now settled from a primary source: the CreateCoreWebView2EnvironmentWithOptions reference (webview2-idl, ms.date 2026-09-21) says WebView creation 'fails with HRESULT_FROM_WIN32(ERROR_INVALID_STATE) if the specified options does not match the options of the WebViews that are currently running in the shared browser process.' The UDF page (ms.date 2026-06-26, updated 2026-09-02) confirms the other quotes word for word. It adds that a UDF can be shared only within one logon session, 'only one HDESKTOP'. That InPrivate cookies are shared between two incognito windows in the same UDF is still untested.

Additional evidence: tauri 2.12.5 webview/mod.rs:2080 rejects an IPC call when `(plugin_command.is_some() || has_app_acl_manifest || !is_local) && resolved_acl.is_none()`, so even app-defined commands are refused from a remote origin unless a capability allows them. One caveat on the polling design: cookies_for_url panics if the login window has already been closed (see the missed items). Poll with cookies() and filter, or check the window first.

Re-read today. MultiBloxy Program.cs has mutexName = "ROBLOX_singletonEvent" and creates a System.Threading.Mutex with it. Named mutexes and events share one kernel namespace, so a pre-created Mutex with that name blocks Roblox's CreateEvent of the same name. Bloxstrap LaunchHandler.cs calls Mutex.TryOpenExisting("ROBLOX_singletonMutex") only for its confirm-launch prompt, and its own comment calls that check unreliable. Which object current RobloxPlayerBeta checks is still unverified. In windows 0.62.2 the success path of CreateMutexW does not touch the thread's last error, so GetLastError() right after the call is valid.

missed.claim: Webview::cookies_for_url() panics instead of returning an error if the target webview or window is already gone, for example when the user closes the login window while a worker is polling. cookies() does not have this problem.
missed.detail: tauri-runtime-wry 2.12.3 lib.rs:1683-1692: `fn cookies_for_url(...) { let (tx, rx) = channel(); self.context.send_user_message(...WebviewMessage::CookiesForUrl(url, tx))?; rx.recv().unwrap() }`. The handler (lib.rs:3643-3649) only runs `if let Some((Some(window), Some(webview))) = webview_handle`. If the webview is missing, the message and its tx are dropped, so recv() returns Err and unwrap() panics on the polling thread. cookies() goes through webview_getter!/getter!, which maps a recv failure to Error::FailedToReceiveMessage (lib.rs:196-232). Design fix: poll with webview.cookies() and filter by name and domain, or check app.get_webview_window(label) first and run the call under std::panic::catch_unwind. Also, both calls turn every WebView2 error into Error::FailedToSendMessage (the HRESULT is lost), and wry's cookie_from_win32 skips cookies it cannot convert without reporting it (wry mod.rs:1734).

missed.claim: Environment variables and Edge policy registry values can silently override each window's data_directory and append browser arguments. That can break per-account isolation or expose cookies, for example by adding --remote-debugging-port.
missed.detail: Microsoft's CreateCoreWebView2EnvironmentWithOptions reference (ms.date 2026-09-21): 'The browserExecutableFolder, channelSearchKind, releaseChannels, userDataFolder and additionalBrowserArguments of the environmentOptions may be overridden by values either specified in environment variables or in the registry.' The variables are WEBVIEW2_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE_FOLDER, WEBVIEW2_USER_DATA_FOLDER, WEBVIEW2_ADDITIONAL_BROWSER_ARGUMENTS, WEBVIEW2_CHANNEL_SEARCH_KIND and WEBVIEW2_RELEASE_CHANNELS. A user data folder value replaces the parameter, and additional arguments are appended. The registry is checked (HKLM, then HKCU, under Software\Policies\Microsoft\Edge\WebView2\{BrowserExecutableFolder,ChannelSearchKind,ReleaseChannels,AdditionalBrowserArguments,UserDataFolder}) when none of the variables are set. If WEBVIEW2_USER_DATA_FOLDER is set, every login-<uuid> window collapses into one shared UDF. Mitigation: clear these variables at the very start of main(), before tauri::Builder (std::env::remove_var is unsafe in edition 2024, so call it single-threaded before the runtime starts). After creating each login window, read pv.environment().cast::<ICoreWebView2Environment7>()?.UserDataFolder() through with_webview, compare it with the expected path, and refuse to continue if they differ. Optionally check for the policy keys and warn.

missed.claim: A WebView2 user data folder can only be shared within one logon session and one desktop (HDESKTOP). This matters for the user's practice of running GUI tests on a hidden Windows desktop.
missed.detail: Microsoft UDF doc: 'a UDF may only be shared among host apps that are in the same logon session (more specifically, only one HDESKTOP).' A RoALT test instance on a hidden desktop must not point at the same app_local_data_dir UDF as an instance running on the user's visible desktop. Give test runs an isolated data root, the same pattern as OPTIMA_DATA_DIR for Optima, or WebView2 environment creation can fail.
crates.io: 1.54.0 (2026-10-19) has yanked=true; 1.54.1 (2026-10-21, MSRV 1.85) is fine. Use tokio = "1.54.1" or later in Cargo.toml so a stale lockfile cannot resolve to the yanked version.

missed.claim: Tauri's set_cookie and delete_cookie report success even when the target webview no longer exists, not only when WebView2 rejects the cookie.
missed.detail: tauri-runtime-wry lib.rs:1698-1714 returns Ok(()) right after send_user_message. If the window or webview lookup at lib.rs:3643-3649 fails, the SetCookie or DeleteCookie message is dropped with no log at all. This is another reason to do injection and deletion through with_webview and the raw ICoreWebView2CookieManager, where the HRESULT is returned to the caller.
